item2.note_text:
# A re-render is **not byte-identical**, by construction (U5.31).  Two
# deliberate effects make it so: :func:`_append_history` *appends* a new block
# to ``HISTORY.md`` (the append-only audit log -- never rewritten), and
# :func:`_preserve_item` writes the outgoing ``ITEM.md`` as a fresh
# ``ITEM.md.rN`` snapshot.  That rotation is **destructive**: it keeps only the
# newest :data:`ITEM_SNAPSHOT_KEEP` = 5 snapshots, so once the window is full
# each render also *deletes the oldest* ``ITEM.md.rN`` (V5.30 measured
# r5 -> r6 (+ delete r1) -> r7 (+ delete r2), banner files +1 per run while the
# manifest sha stayed fixed).  A verifier diffing a re-rendered docket must
# therefore expect a new ``HISTORY.md`` block, one new ``ITEM.md.rN``, and the
# loss of the oldest snapshot; byte identity across renders is not a contract.
item2.proof_detail: stripping the inserted # comment block reproduces the pre-edit bytes exactly (sha 8cb9af52...), ast.dump(parse(cur))==ast.dump(parse(stripped)) is True, and the compiled module code objects are identical (co_code/co_names/co_varnames/co_argcount/co_flags)
item2.should_be_idempotent_instead: no - the append-only HISTORY.md audit log is deliberate; forcing byte-identity would either rewrite/lose the audit trail or drop the ITEM.md snapshot window, both changing delivery semantics on the real dockets. The destructive rotation is now documented instead (V5.30's measurement).
